title: Team Coupling Thermostat and Commitment Safehouse
creator: Avery Chen
description: Problem: We frequently discover high-coupling blockers late in the cycle (design handoffs, infra capacity, security reviews) that cause scope slippage and fire-drill work. Goal: Provide a lightweight, automated visibility and remediation layer that quantifies coupling risk across Eng/Design/Security/Infra and provides a ‘safehouse’ escrow for commitments with clear remediation windows and escalation paths. Deliverables: 1) Team Coupling Thermostat metric (coupling score per initiative) computed from ownership signals, open blockers, API surface changes, infra footprint, and required security gates; 2) Commitment Safehouse — a ticketing/escrow pattern where a team can temporarily escrow a dependent deliverable with acceptance criteria, mitigation plan, and rollback triggers; 3) UI/alerts in the Console & Roadmap dashboard, plus automated Slack/Email nudges and a weekly coupling report for PM/EM reviews.
acceptance_criteria: Thermostat score computed for 95% of active initiatives in the current quarter using available signals
Escrow ticket template integrated with Linear and linked to parent initiative with automated reminders
Console dashboard shows top-10 coupling hotspots with filters by team and risk level
Escalation flow (pager/owner -> technical lead -> PM -> VP) documented and tested in a dry-run
Spike tests show coupling score correlates with historical slippage for a sample of 12 initiatives (precision > 0.6)
tasks: Define coupling score components and weighting (signals: blockers, API churn, infra footprint, security gates)
Implement signal collectors: GitHub label scraper, Jira/Linear blocker extractor, infra capacity hook, security-review flag integration
Design escrow ticket schema and default mitigation fields
Build prototype dashboard widget in Console (mock in Figma -> dev implementation)
Add alert rules and Slack workflow for high-coupling: <team>-readiness channel
Run two dry-runs with cross-functional squads and capture feedback
Write runbook and acceptance checklist for on-call and PM triage

notes: Trade-offs: a high-sensitivity thermostat will increase noise and interrupt teams frequently; we plan a phased rollout (observability-only -> soft alerts -> enforced escrow). Monitoring plan includes false-positive rate and feedback survey after two sprints. Ops will own the escalation runbook; PMs own the mitigation plans.
